statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. The Nasdaq-100 complex is inside the CME weekend halt, so no quoting price path exists in any published hour and Tail is held at a closed-venue floor.
recommendation: Tail stays far below the block threshold at a closed-venue floor of 4-5%, so the deterministic mapping holds EA_ON and green across all 24 published hours. Stress drifts from 39% to 47%, crossing into the elevated band from 04:00 UTC on 6 September, to reflect hawkish September rate pricing and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium carried unpriced across the halt. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: Nasdaq-100 unquoted at 29,544.15 through the CME weekend halt; the full 24-hour horizon ends about thirteen hours before the Sunday restart, so Tail holds a closed-venue floor while hawkish September rate pricing and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium accumulate unpriced
body: The Nasdaq-100 closed the August payroll session on Friday 4 September at 29,544.15, up 61.85 points or 0.21% from a 29,482.30 previous close, having ranged between 29,440.15 and 29,655.22. Price retraced repeatedly in both directions during that session, which is the opposite of the persistent no-retracement structure the Tail score measures. The Bureau of Labor Statistics Employment Situation release shows August nonfarm payrolls up 162,000 against a consensus near 56,000, the unemployment rate unchanged at 4.1%, average hourly earnings up 0.3% on the month to $37.75 and 3.1% on the year, and upward revisions of 55,000 across June and July. Reuters reported the priced probability of a quarter-point increase at the 15-16 September FOMC meeting at 58.4%, up from 49.4% the previous day, while the H.15 release confirms the two-year Treasury yield at 4.34% and the ten-year at 4.77% through 3 September. Index internals were split rather than aligned: the Nasdaq-100 rose while the S&P 500 and Dow closed lower, with the narrow index carried by semiconductor and memory leadership against megacap weakness. Conflicting internals of that kind reduce directional conviction and lift Stress; they are not evidence of the one-way path Tail is defined against. The VIX settled at 14.53 inside a 13.80-14.58 range, indicating the options market did not price disorderly repricing even on a hot payroll day. The material unpriced input remains energy: WTI settled at $91.48, roughly 9% higher on the week and 21.6% higher on the month, against a Strait of Hormuz crisis that produced repeated verified vessel strikes through late August and US strikes on IRGC targets on 1 September. All of that is carried across the CME weekend halt, which began at 21:00 UTC on Friday and runs to 22:00 UTC on Sunday, about thirteen hours beyond the final hour published here. Because no Nasdaq-100 price path can form inside any published hour, Tail is held at a closed-venue floor of 4-5% and the deterministic mapping stays EA_ON and green throughout, while Stress drifts from 39% to 47% to carry the accumulating unpriced risk.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours cover the second half of the August payroll session and the first fifteen hours of the CME weekend halt. Tail ran 17% with Stress at 62% through the final pre-release hour, peaked at Tail 24% and Stress 76% in the 12:00 UTC release hour under an event/whipsaw mode as the 162,000 payroll print landed against a consensus near 56,000, then decayed steadily through the US cash session as the index retraced its highs and recovered. Mode moved to mixed from 15:00 UTC as semiconductor leadership diverged from a softer broad tape, and by 20:00 UTC Tail was 12% with Stress at 48%. From the 21:00 UTC CME settle the assessment moved to a closed-venue floor of Tail 5% and Stress 38%, held unchanged through the overnight and Saturday morning hours. No hour required a mapped state beyond WATCH, and no hour recorded the persistent one-way structure that Tail is calibrated against.
outlookSummary: The entire 24-hour horizon falls inside the CME weekend halt, so no observable Nasdaq-100 price path can form in any published hour and the mapped policy state stays EA_ON throughout. Tail is held at a 4-5% closed-venue floor, easing to 4% through the dormant middle of the weekend and returning to 5% as the horizon tracks back toward the venue timeline. Stress drifts from 39% to 47%, crossing into the elevated band from 04:00 UTC on 6 September, reflecting hawkish September rate pricing after Friday's payroll beat and a Strait of Hormuz energy premium that lifted crude roughly 9% on the week and is carried unpriced across the halt. Confidence decays from 85% to 76% as Friday's verified evidence ages with no means of refreshing price-path observation. The Sunday 22:00 UTC restart, the Monday 7 September US Labor Day closure, and the PPI and CPI releases on 10 and 11 September all fall beyond the final published hour and will be scored by later cycles against live evidence.
